The vocabulary: one table, five functions, one field

The template types are as on main: no new body kind, no new variable field. What is new under representation/ is projectId on every template, a set term a variable's default may carry, the templateStages table, four pure functions under data/behavior/templates/ (resolve variable scopes through answers then defaults; make a live body portable; mint fresh ids into a fragment; take one slide out of a deck as a deck) and one under behavior/core/ (resolve a resource set against a catalogue), and Target.context, which lets a tab be opened straight onto a named context view. The workspace-state methods that honour that field sit with it here.

2

The templates capability

Every procedure now works over the project's templates rather than a viewer's own, and nothing is owner-only. Five procedures are new: a resource becomes a template, a template is opened into a scratch resource, saved back from it, the copy is discarded, and a resource is asked what it is. Three changed: instantiate accepts caller answers and falls back to each variable's default; update can replace the variable list and carries the template's stage to the revision it makes; remove discards the stage and versions with the template and touches no resource, because none refers back; instantiate stamps nothing on the resource it makes and records the template's last use instead. The validator accepts a note on a URL link and a set term in a default, and the shared body helpers moved to the representation. The comments capability gained one refusal: no thread on a working copy.

3

The resource-sets capability

New. The table existed and was seeded; nothing read it. Four procedures: read the project's sets with a live count each, create, update by compare-and-swap, remove while no other set and no template variable's default names it.

@@ -0,0 +1,27 @@+# resource-sets++The project's resource sets: the scopes a prompt looks things up in.++| procedure | answers |+| --- | --- |+| `readResourceSets` | Every valid **named** set in the scoped project, with its creator's name and how many resources it selects now, plus quarantined invalid rows |+| `createResourceSet` | A set from a name, an optional description, and an include and exclude list |+| `updateResourceSet` | A compare-and-swap change to name, description, or the set itself |+| `removeResourceSet` | A compare-and-swap delete, refused while another set or a template hole's default in this project still names it |++A set is `include` minus `exclude`. A term selects the whole project, a list of+resource kinds matched by segment, named resources, or another set by id. The+count each set reports is resolved when it is read, over the documents, decks,+spreadsheets, findings and research threads the project holds — never stored,+so it cannot go stale. A template's staged copy is left out of that catalogue.++**A row carries a name or an owner, and never both or neither.** A named row is+a project subject: people make it here, it is listed here, and every builder+offers it. A row with `boundTo` instead is a value something else holds, written+because the rule could not be said inline — it is never listed, never named, and+goes when its owner goes. These procedures only ever make and change named rows;+the bound ones belong to whichever capability owns the thing that points at them.++Every stored row is re-admitted before projection or mutation. A malformed row+is quarantined from the list and refused by update and remove, so one corrupt+row cannot take the rest down. A set that would include itself is refused.

4

What the other capabilities changed

Project resources gained one exclusion: the index reads the project's stage rows first and skips the resources they occupy, so a working copy never appears in Project Overview, in New Tab's recents, or in the comment picker. Comments gained one refusal: startThread reads the stage table and refuses a target one of its rows names, because a comment does not travel with a template. The store's document lost a sentence naming documents.templateId, a field that no longer exists.

The template library, editor door, and inspector

Double-click and an Edit action open the template's copy in its editor, landed on the Templates panel; the editor door does the same and returns to the library; each variable in the inspector shows its description and a Default that opens the modal. Nothing marks a template as being edited.

6

The document editor's Templates panel

The eight-line placeholder became the panel: a name and Save for an ordinary document; Save to template, Discard, the template band and the variables for a stage; every document template behind a search, each row with Insert and Edit. Insert opens one modal that asks what each variable should select, its default first. The procedure module computes insertion ops, answers, variable rules and defaults without a browser.

9

The seeded one-slide template

One deck template holding a single slide, Section divider, so a fresh seed has a one-slide template to list and the browser test can insert one without first making it; and every seeded template names the project it belongs to.

11

The reference pages, and the one shared component they moved

The two pages in the app that describe this work — how templates work, and what changed — are a development view mounted at two routes, with a script that regenerates the file ledger from the working tree against the branch point. One shared component moved with them: a panel section that starts open used to mount its body in the tick that mounted its heading, which left the disclosure primitive reading a derived from the destroyed tick once the panel was torn down, and every browser specification fails on a console warning.

Every file in this change

What to know before merging

  • Every change is in the working tree, uncommitted on work/template-features; no git command beyond creating the worktree was run.
  • The 47 changed files are where a conflict could arise; the 46 new files cannot.
  • Main has moved three commits since the branch point — now 47f2981: document-editor and slide-deck-editor stabilization, and the editor-audit pages, 102 files under app/. Ten of them are files this work also changed: seed/templates.json, seed/templateVersions.json, document-editor/content/document.svelte, slide-deck-editor/context/comments.svelte, slide-deck-editor/inspector/threads.svelte, slide-deck-editor/slide-deck-editor.md, templates/api/instantiate-template/instantiate-template.ts, templates/api/shared/validation.ts, templates/test/unit/templates.test.ts and test/browser/document-editor.spec.ts. Four of those matter to a merge: main now normalizes a document's legacy line height and readies a deck body inside instantiateTemplate (keep both calls when the files are merged), admits strikethrough on a text style, rewrote the seeded line heights from multipliers to points, and its instantiation test asserts the templateId provenance this work removes — that assertion is the one place the two sides disagree rather than merely overlap.
  • Four contracts changed shape on main's side: representation/store/tables.ts (templates.projectId required and lastUsedAt optional, so every stored template row and the seed carry the project; templateId removed from documents, decks and spreadsheets, and from the seeded rows), representation/data/types/core/resource-set.ts (a set term on TemplatedTerm), capabilities/templates/types/templates.ts (instantiate takes answers; new procedures; no forbidden or in-use-elsewhere refusal; no madeFrom) and representation/data/types/workspace/tab.ts (Target.context, optional). Everything that read the old shapes still typechecks.
  • Verification after the last edit: typecheck 0 errors across 2443 files; lint 56 checks clean; 857 unit tests in 89 files; browser 22 of 23, the one failure being the deck spec's shift-click case, which fails identically on main.
  • Rebuild this page with nix develop ./infra/devshell --command node docs/reference/template-features/build-diffs.mjs from the worktree root; it rewrites the reference suite's dropdowns, this page and its markdown mirror in one pass.
Companion pages: the reference suite under docs/reference/template-features/, and the three artifacts Template Dictionary, Stages, Sets and Variables and Template Stage Flow, mirrored under docs/artifacts/.
